items.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: At one point Benny Carter wanted to hire him... Benny Carter wanted to hire him, because he was the house band in the ghetto section of Las Vegas.

ctx.x: Date. Give me a date. Are we in the late ’40s now? mid-’40s? Where are we time-wise?

I think we’re in the late ’40s, because I left – I didn’t leave town until the ’50s. So it’s got to be between ’45 and the ’50s. Got to be in there, because I remember being out there. The dates, you know, I guess I’m an old guy now. I can’t really think of when the dates – pigeonhole where the dates are, but it had to be in that area. So, yeah, Fats was pretty close, because he used to live pretty close to that. I remember him walking from his house to my house. He was a fat dude. He wore out a pair of pants.…
Did he come out of a – was he in a service band or something? Did he have that background?

items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: And Jimmy, you're stringing me up.

ctx.x: that I noticed about some of those methods; that is, that they will give you chord progressions, and here's a line...
